# Restricting and completing global polynomial-pair measurements

The combining map embeds pairs of bounded individual-degree polynomials into
extended polynomials. Restricting a measurement along this embedding produces a
submeasurement whose missing operator is the sum of the noncombined effects.
Relabeling those effects by one specified pair completes the measurement and
preserves projectivity.

These algebraic constructions do not establish the concentration estimate
`eq:qld-g-non-separable` or the point consistency required by
`exists_globalPairWitness`. Issue #513 retains those obligations.

## References

- Blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`.
- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1375-1404`,
  `eq:qld-sgg-completeness` and the final completion paragraph.
- Restriction and completion proofs recovered from commit `cb6d86d8`;
  the evaluation identity is from `3de03d0a`, as preserved at `aaa5cb48`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder

noncomputable section

/-- Recover the two polynomial components by setting the unused block to zero
and the scalar coordinates to `(1,0)` or `(0,1)`. This algebraic substitution
is the left inverse implicit in the restriction to combined outcomes in
`eq:qld-sgg-completeness`, paper lines 1375--1380. Unlike evaluation as a
polynomial function on a finite field, it does not require a degree bound. -/
noncomputable def recoverCombinedPair {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m : ℕ}
    (polynomial : MvPolynomial (Fin (2 * m + 2)) K) :
    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K × MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
  (MvPolynomial.eval₂ MvPolynomial.C (fun index =>
    match finCombineEquiv m index with
    | .inl (.inl coordinate) => MvPolynomial.X coordinate
    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
    | .inr scalar => if scalar = 0 then 1 else 0) polynomial,
   MvPolynomial.eval₂ MvPolynomial.C (fun index =>
    match finCombineEquiv m index with
    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
    | .inl (.inr coordinate) => MvPolynomial.X coordinate
    | .inr scalar => if scalar = 1 then 1 else 0) polynomial)

/-- Substitution recovers both components of a combined polynomial. This is
formalization support for the relabeling in `eq:qld-sgg-completeness`, paper
lines 1375--1380. -/
@[simp] theorem recoverCombinedPair_combinePoly {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m : ℕ}
    (first second : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) :
    recoverCombinedPair (combinePoly first second) = (first, second) := by
  simp [recoverCombinedPair, combinePoly, MvPolynomial.eval₂_rename,
    embX, embZ, alphaVar, betaVar, Function.comp_def, MvPolynomial.eval₂_eta]

/-- Distinct polynomial pairs label distinct combined outcomes. This justifies
restricting a measurement on extended polynomials to pairs without duplicating
an effect in `eq:qld-sgg-completeness`, paper lines 1375--1380. -/
theorem combinePoly_injective {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m : ℕ} :
    Function.Injective (fun pair : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K × MvPolynomial (Fin m) K =>
      combinePoly pair.1 pair.2) := by
  exact (show Function.LeftInverse recoverCombinedPair
    (fun pair : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K × MvPolynomial (Fin m) K =>
      combinePoly pair.1 pair.2) from fun pair =>
        recoverCombinedPair_combinePoly pair.1 pair.2).injective

/-- The bounded polynomial-pair embedding used to restrict the global
measurement in `eq:qld-sgg-completeness`, paper lines 1375--1380. The degree
bound is inherited from `def:combine-map`; the two scalar coordinates have
degree one, allowed by admissibility. -/
noncomputable def combinedPolyEmbedding (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    PolyPair P ↪ MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc (2 * P.m + 2) (PauliScalar P) P.d where
  toFun pair := ⟨combinePoly pair.1.1 pair.2.1,
    combinePoly_mem_polyFunc P.hd pair.1.2 pair.2.2⟩
  inj' := by
    intro first second heq
    have hpoly : combinePoly first.1.1 first.2.1 = combinePoly second.1.1 second.2.1 :=
      congrArg Subtype.val heq
    have hpair : (first.1.1, first.2.1) = (second.1.1, second.2.1) :=
      combinePoly_injective hpoly
    exact Prod.ext (Subtype.ext (congrArg Prod.fst hpair))
      (Subtype.ext (congrArg Prod.snd hpair))

/-- Evaluation of a combined outcome is the affine combination of its two
components.  This is the pointwise algebraic identity used when transferring
the global-pair measurement to the expanded point measurements in
`lem:qld-4-7`, paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1364--1380`.
It is a formalization-only consequence of `def:combine-map`; it does not assert
any consistency or quantitative error estimate.
-/
theorem combinedPolyEmbedding_eval (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → PauliScalar P) (pair : PolyPair P) :
    MvPolynomial.eval u (combinedPolyEmbedding P pair).1 =
      u (alphaVar P.m) * evalAt .X (projX u) pair +
        u (betaVar P.m) * evalAt .Z (projZ u) pair := by
  change MvPolynomial.eval u (combinePoly pair.1.1 pair.2.1) = _
  rw [combinePoly_eval]
  rfl

/-- Restrict an extended-polynomial measurement to combined outcomes, as in
`eq:qld-sgg-completeness`, paper lines 1375--1380. Injectivity of the combining
map ensures that the retained effects sum to at most the identity. This
construction does not assert the source's quantitative completeness bound. -/
noncomputable def combinedPairSubmeasurement (P : AdmissibleParams)
    {carrier : Type*} [Fintype carrier] [DecidableEq carrier]
    (measurement : Quantum.Measurement
      (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc (2 * P.m + 2) (PauliScalar P) P.d) carrier) :
    Quantum.Submeasurement (PolyPair P) carrier where
  effect pair := measurement.effect (combinedPolyEmbedding P pair)
  pos pair := measurement.pos _
  sum_le_one := by
    classical
    rw [← Finset.sum_image (fun first _ second _ heq =>
      (combinedPolyEmbedding P).injective heq)]
    exact (Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _)
      (fun outcome _ _ => measurement.pos outcome)).trans measurement.sum_le_one

/-- Restricting to combined outcomes preserves projectivity, as asserted
before `eq:qld-sgg-completeness`, paper lines 1375--1380. -/
theorem combinedPairSubmeasurement_projective (P : AdmissibleParams)
    {carrier : Type*} [Fintype carrier] [DecidableEq carrier]
    (measurement : Quantum.Measurement
      (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc (2 * P.m + 2) (PauliScalar P) P.d) carrier)
    (hprojective : Measurement.IsProjective measurement) :
    ∀ pair, Quantum.IsProj ((combinedPairSubmeasurement P measurement).effect pair) := by
  intro pair
  exact hprojective (combinedPolyEmbedding P pair)

/-- The missing operator of the polynomial-pair submeasurement is exactly the
sum of the effects outside the range of the combining map. This is the
operator identity underlying `eq:qld-sgg-completeness`, paper lines 1375--1380;
the bound on its state mass is a separate obligation. -/
theorem combinedPairSubmeasurement_missing (P : AdmissibleParams)
    {carrier : Type*} [Fintype carrier] [DecidableEq carrier]
    (measurement : Quantum.Measurement
      (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc (2 * P.m + 2) (PauliScalar P) P.d) carrier) :
    1 - (combinedPairSubmeasurement P measurement).total =
      ∑ polynomial ∈ Finset.univ.filter
        (fun polynomial => polynomial ∉ Set.range (combinedPolyEmbedding P)),
        measurement.effect polynomial := by
  classical
  have htotal : (combinedPairSubmeasurement P measurement).total =
      ∑ polynomial ∈ Finset.univ.filter
        (fun polynomial => polynomial ∈ Set.range (combinedPolyEmbedding P)),
        measurement.effect polynomial := by
    change (∑ pair, measurement.effect (combinedPolyEmbedding P pair)) = _
    rw [← Finset.sum_image (fun first _ second _ heq =>
      (combinedPolyEmbedding P).injective heq)]
    congr 1
    ext polynomial
    simp
  rw [htotal, ← measurement.sum_eq_one]
  apply sub_eq_iff_eq_add.mpr
  exact (Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not Finset.univ
    (fun polynomial => polynomial ∈ Set.range (combinedPolyEmbedding P))
    measurement.effect).symm.trans (add_comm _ _)

/-- Relabel a combined polynomial by its unique pair and send every other
polynomial to a specified pair. This implements the completion at an arbitrary
outcome in the last paragraph of `lem:qld-4-7`, paper lines 1402--1404. The
noncombined outcomes are retained at the completion outcome, not discarded. -/
noncomputable def completedPairLabel (P : AdmissibleParams) (completionPair : PolyPair P) :
    MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc (2 * P.m + 2) (PauliScalar P) P.d → PolyPair P :=
  Function.extend (combinedPolyEmbedding P) id (fun _ => completionPair)

/-- Completion preserves every combined polynomial's pair label. -/
@[simp] theorem completedPairLabel_combinedPolyEmbedding (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (completionPair pair : PolyPair P) :
    completedPairLabel P completionPair (combinedPolyEmbedding P pair) = pair := by
  exact (combinedPolyEmbedding P).injective.extend_apply _ _ _

/-- All outcomes outside the combining map's range go to the completion pair. -/
theorem completedPairLabel_of_not_mem_range (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (completionPair : PolyPair P)
    (polynomial : MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc (2 * P.m + 2) (PauliScalar P) P.d)
    (houtside : polynomial ∉ Set.range (combinedPolyEmbedding P)) :
    completedPairLabel P completionPair polynomial = completionPair := by
  exact Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ houtside

/-- The completed polynomial-pair measurement of the final paragraph of
`lem:qld-4-7`, paper lines 1402--1404, obtained by relabeling all extended
polynomial outcomes. No assertion about consistency is built into this
construction. -/
noncomputable def completedPairMeasurement (P : AdmissibleParams)
    {carrier : Type*} [Fintype carrier] [DecidableEq carrier]
    (measurement : Quantum.Measurement
      (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc (2 * P.m + 2) (PauliScalar P) P.d) carrier)
    (completionPair : PolyPair P) : Quantum.Measurement (PolyPair P) carrier :=
  measurement.postprocess (completedPairLabel P completionPair)

/-- Completing the pair measurement adds precisely its missing operator to
the specified outcome and leaves all other effects unchanged. This is the
completion formula of `lem:qld-4-7`, paper lines 1402--1404. -/
theorem completedPairMeasurement_effect (P : AdmissibleParams)
    {carrier : Type*} [Fintype carrier] [DecidableEq carrier]
    (measurement : Quantum.Measurement
      (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc (2 * P.m + 2) (PauliScalar P) P.d) carrier)
    (completionPair pair : PolyPair P) :
    (completedPairMeasurement P measurement completionPair).effect pair =
      (combinedPairSubmeasurement P measurement).effect pair +
        if pair = completionPair then 1 - (combinedPairSubmeasurement P measurement).total
        else 0 := by
  classical
  rw [completedPairMeasurement, Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter]
  rw [← Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not Finset.univ
    (fun polynomial => polynomial ∈ Set.range (combinedPolyEmbedding P))]
  have hgood :
      Finset.univ.filter (fun polynomial => polynomial ∈ Set.range (combinedPolyEmbedding P)) =
        Finset.univ.image (combinedPolyEmbedding P) := by
    ext polynomial
    simp
  rw [hgood, Finset.sum_image (fun first _ second _ heq =>
    (combinedPolyEmbedding P).injective heq)]
  simp only [completedPairLabel_combinedPolyEmbedding]
  rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq', if_pos (Finset.mem_univ pair)]
  congr 1
  have hbad :
      (∑ polynomial ∈ Finset.univ.filter
        (fun polynomial => polynomial ∉ Set.range (combinedPolyEmbedding P)),
        if completedPairLabel P completionPair polynomial = pair then
          measurement.effect polynomial else 0) =
      ∑ polynomial ∈ Finset.univ.filter
        (fun polynomial => polynomial ∉ Set.range (combinedPolyEmbedding P)),
        if completionPair = pair then measurement.effect polynomial else 0 := by
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro polynomial hpolynomial
    rw [completedPairLabel_of_not_mem_range P completionPair polynomial
      (Finset.mem_filter.mp hpolynomial).2]
  rw [hbad]
  by_cases heq : pair = completionPair
  · simp [heq, combinedPairSubmeasurement_missing]
  · simp [heq, Ne.symm heq]

/-- The completed polynomial-pair measurement is projective whenever the
extended-polynomial measurement is projective. This proves the qualitative
completion step in `lem:qld-4-7`, paper lines 1402--1404, without assuming its
unproved consistency conclusion. -/
theorem completedPairMeasurement_projective (P : AdmissibleParams)
    {carrier : Type*} [Fintype carrier] [DecidableEq carrier]
    (measurement : Quantum.Measurement
      (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc (2 * P.m + 2) (PauliScalar P) P.d) carrier)
    (hprojective : Measurement.IsProjective measurement) (completionPair : PolyPair P) :
    Measurement.IsProjective (completedPairMeasurement P measurement completionPair) := by
  exact SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective measurement hprojective _

open MIPStarRE.Quantum DistanceCalculus

/-- Completion can only increase agreement with any evaluated reference
measurement on the opposite tensor factor. Consequently, its consistency
defect is at most the squared state norm minus the retained diagonal overlap.
This is the completion step of `lem:qld-4-7`, paper lines 1402--1404, for an
arbitrary outcome evaluation; it does not supply the preceding overlap bound.
Neither projectivity nor normalization of the state is needed. -/
theorem completedPairMeasurement_evaluated_defect_le (P : AdmissibleParams)
    {Answer Left Right : Type*} [Fintype Answer] [DecidableEq Answer]
    [Fintype Left] [DecidableEq Left] [Fintype Right] [DecidableEq Right]
    (measurement : Quantum.Measurement
      (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc (2 * P.m + 2) (PauliScalar P) P.d) Left)
    (completionPair : PolyPair P) (eval : PolyPair P → Answer)
    (reference : Quantum.Measurement Answer Right)
    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Left × Right)) :
    (∑ a : Answer, ∑ b : Answer, if a = b then 0 else
      stateQForm psi (heteroKron
        (((completedPairMeasurement P measurement completionPair).postprocess eval).effect a)
        (reference.effect b))) ≤
      ‖psi‖ ^ 2 - ∑ pair : PolyPair P, stateQForm psi
        (heteroKron ((combinedPairSubmeasurement P measurement).effect pair)
          (reference.effect (eval pair))) := by
  classical
  let completed := completedPairMeasurement P measurement completionPair
  have hdiag :
      (∑ a : Answer, stateQForm psi
        (heteroKron ((completed.postprocess eval).effect a) (reference.effect a))) =
        ∑ pair : PolyPair P, stateQForm psi
          (heteroKron (completed.effect pair) (reference.effect (eval pair))) := by
    simp_rw [Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, heteroKron_finset_sum_left,
      stateQForm_finset_sum]
    calc
      _ = ∑ a : Answer, ∑ pair ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun pair => eval pair = a),
          stateQForm psi
            (heteroKron (completed.effect pair) (reference.effect (eval pair))) := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro a _
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro pair hpair
        rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp hpair).2]
      _ = _ := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ eval _
  have hretained :
      (∑ pair : PolyPair P, stateQForm psi
        (heteroKron ((combinedPairSubmeasurement P measurement).effect pair)
          (reference.effect (eval pair)))) ≤
        ∑ pair : PolyPair P, stateQForm psi
          (heteroKron (completed.effect pair) (reference.effect (eval pair))) := by
    apply Finset.sum_le_sum
    intro pair _
    dsimp [completed]
    rw [completedPairMeasurement_effect]
    by_cases hpair : pair = completionPair
    · rw [if_pos hpair, heteroKron_add_left, stateQForm_add]
      exact le_add_of_nonneg_right (stateQForm_nonneg psi
        (kronecker_nonneg
          (sub_nonneg.mpr (combinedPairSubmeasurement P measurement).total_le_one)
          (reference.pos (eval pair))))
    · simp [hpair]
  have hdefect := point_defect_eq
    (leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := Right) (completed.postprocess eval))
    (rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := Left) reference) psi
  simp only [leftPlacedMeasurement, rightPlacedMeasurement,
    Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne] at hdefect
  simp_rw [placed_product_stateQForm_eq] at hdefect
  change _ ≤ _
  rw [hdefect, hdiag]
  exact sub_le_sub_left hretained _

/-- Uniformly averaging the completion estimate gives the consistency defect
needed for the point marginals in `lem:qld-4-7`, paper lines 1402--1404.
The retained overlap remains explicit and must be bounded from the source
strategy before this estimate can establish global-pair existence. -/
theorem completedPairMeasurement_consistencyDefect_le (P : AdmissibleParams)
    {Question Answer Left Right : Type*}
    [Fintype Question] [DecidableEq Question] [Nonempty Question]
    [Fintype Answer] [DecidableEq Answer]
    [Fintype Left] [DecidableEq Left] [Fintype Right] [DecidableEq Right]
    (measurement : Quantum.Measurement
      (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc (2 * P.m + 2) (PauliScalar P) P.d) Left)
    (completionPair : PolyPair P) (eval : Question → PolyPair P → Answer)
    (reference : Question → Quantum.Measurement Answer Right)
    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Left × Right)) :
    consistencyDefect (MIPStarRE.LDT.uniformDistribution Question)
      (fun x a => heteroKron
        (((completedPairMeasurement P measurement completionPair).postprocess (eval x)).effect a)
        (1 : Op Right))
      (fun x a => heteroKron (1 : Op Left) ((reference x).effect a)) psi ≤
      ‖psi‖ ^ 2 - MIPStarRE.LDT.avgOver (MIPStarRE.LDT.uniformDistribution Question)
        (fun x => ∑ pair : PolyPair P, stateQForm psi
          (heteroKron ((combinedPairSubmeasurement P measurement).effect pair)
            ((reference x).effect (eval x pair)))) := by
  rw [SandwichProduct.consistencyDefect_placed_eq_avg_point]
  have h := MIPStarRE.LDT.avgOver_mono (MIPStarRE.LDT.uniformDistribution Question) _ _
    (fun x => completedPairMeasurement_evaluated_defect_le P measurement completionPair
      (eval x) (reference x) psi)
  simpa only [MIPStarRE.LDT.avgOver_sub, MIPStarRE.LDT.avgOver_uniform_const] using h

end

The two-tier split\\n\\n`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and\\ndifferent sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the\\nparent's failure.\\n\\nAn absolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` relocates `.lake` to `<root>/<branch>` for a\\none-component branch name. The helper rejects `/`, symlink targets, escape, and\\ncanonical overlap with packages, `hot-main`, the repository, or any worktree,\\nplus canonical-equal ownership by another worktree. Export it before setup or\\nwarming and through dispatch and cleanup; only its target gets `--add-dir`.\\n\\n**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,\\n`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the\\nparent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and\\ndistributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**\\ncopy.\\n\\n**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The\\nparent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud\\ncache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally they live **once\\nper manifest** in a shared, read-only store:\\n`$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`, `key = sha256(lake-manifest.json ‖ lean-toolchain)[:16]`,\\nand every worktree's `.lake/packages` is a symlink to it.\\n\\n> **Why a shared store is safe here (2026-09-03).** The old objection — a\\n> shared tree is read-only only by convention, so one `lake update` mutates it\\n> for everyone — is answered mechanically: the store is `chmod -R a-w`, so any\\n> write (an automated `lake update`, a dependency rebuild after a manifest\\n> drift) fails loudly in the one worktree that attempted it. Identity is by\\n> key, so a Mathlib bump simply creates a new store entry; worktrees on the old\\n> manifest keep linking the old one. The first worktree to need a key fetches\\n> with `lake exe cache get` into a real directory, then *publishes* it (move,\\n> `chmod a-w`, link); later worktrees only link. Cost: 7.3 GB once per key\\n> instead of per worktree (8 copies = 58 GB on 2026-09-03, on a 97 % full disk).\\n> `worktree-setup.sh` still refuses to run `lake update`.\\n\\nConsequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It\\nrewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under\\nevery published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib\\nbumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3. The cache key\\n\\n```\\nkeyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )\\n```\\n\\nconcatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local\\nanalog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in\\n`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`\\nand `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay\\nbyte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.\\nA missing input file is a hard error, never a default.\\n\\nTwo properties matter, and they are not symmetric:\\n\\n1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's\\n   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest\\n   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is\\n   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash\\n   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not\\n   need their timestamps preserved.\\n2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,\\n   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.\\n   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`\\n   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls\\n   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 4. On-disk layout\\n\\nShared packages and `hot-main` use `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`; branch products may\\nuse `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` as in §2. Neither runtime tree is committed.\\n\\n```\\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/\\n├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time\\n│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose\\n├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends\\n├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)\\n└── hot-main/\\n    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this\\n    │   └── info\\n    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main\\n    ├── snapshots/\\n    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\\n    │   │   ├── STAMP\\n    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build\\n    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\\n    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink\\n```\\n\\nSnapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse\\nlexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`\\ncalls and no name parsing.\\n\\n### `STAMP` schema\\n\\nA flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts\\nparse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase\\nhex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever\\n`eval`ed or `source`d.\\n\\n```\\nsha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>\\nkeyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>\\ntimestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>\\ntimestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>\\nstatus=complete|partial\\nbuild_seconds=<integer>\\ntoolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>\\nsnapshot=<snapshot directory name>\\nwarmer_version=1\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`\\n\\n```\\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]\\n                          [--targets \\\"<lake targets>\\\"] [--lock-timeout S]\\n                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]\\n```\\n\\n### 5.1 Writer lease\\n\\nAcquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic\\ntest-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,\\n`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.\\n\\nStaleness is decided in this order:\\n\\n* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead\\n  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.\\n* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).\\n\\nThe TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this\\nrepository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,\\n2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease\\nmid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to\\nprevent.\\n\\n**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that\\nboth judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;\\n`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and\\nre-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A\\n`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.\\n\\n### 5.2 Build\\n\\n1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`\\n   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.\\n   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and\\n   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).\\n2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).\\n3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**\\n   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and\\n   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,\\n   finish, then warm again.\\n4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply\\n   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.\\n   **No `lake update`.**\\n5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.\\n   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is\\n   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent\\n   prompts may later read.\\n\\n### 5.3 Atomic publish\\n\\nThe publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:\\n\\n1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with\\n   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the\\n   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).\\n2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.\\n3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.\\n   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already\\n   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**\\n4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over\\n   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).\\n\\n> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,\\n> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would\\n> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real\\n> trap, not a hypothetical one.\\n\\nConsumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the\\nresolved concrete path for the rest of the run.\\n\\n### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional\\n\\nIf `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and\\nexits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`\\ncommit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did\\ncompile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say\\nso loudly.\\n\\nA non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *\\\"main did not build cleanly\\\"* —\\nnot *\\\"nothing was published.\\\"* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a\\nreason to retry.\\n\\n### 5.5 Retention\\n\\nKeep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's\\n10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never\\ncollected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has\\nresolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging\\ndirectories older than an hour are swept.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`\\n\\n```\\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]\\n                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]\\n```\\n\\nThe consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to\\noperate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.\\n\\nDecision procedure:\\n\\n1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).\\n2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.\\n3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. A malformed stamp is treated as *no snapshot*.\\n4. **Keyhash gate.** Mismatch → warn with both hashes, name the likely cause\\n   (toolchain / manifest / lakefile change), point at the warmer, and take the\\n   cold path. Never a partial reuse, never a silent skip.\\n5. **Warm path**: `cp -c -R <snapshot>/build → <worktree>/.lake/build.incoming.$$`,\\n   then `rename` into place. Write the idempotency marker\\n   `<worktree>/.lake/.mipstarre-warm-stamp` recording the snapshot name, keyhash,\\n   snapshot status and time. Then fetch tier 2 with `lake exe cache get`.\\n   No full build unless `--build` is given — the point of the warm path is that\\n   the agent's next incremental `lake build` compiles only its own delta.\\n6. **Cold path**: `lake exe cache get`, then a full `lake build` under the\\n   machine-wide lock (§7), unless `--no-build`.\\n\\n### 6.1 Idempotency and the do-not-clobber rule\\n\\nRe-running on an already-warmed worktree is a no-op for tier 1. Specifically:\\n\\n* marker snapshot **and** keyhash both match the resolved snapshot → skip the\\n  clone;\\n* `.lake/build` is populated but was **not** warmed from this snapshot → leave it\\n  alone and warn. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it\\n  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.\\n\\n### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink\\n\\nOn APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near\\ninstantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid\\nfor only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. This is what makes a\\n*private writable copy per worktree* affordable — and a private writable copy is\\nprecisely what preserves the single-writer invariant. A writable symlink or\\nbind-style share of `.lake/build` across two concurrent `lake build` invocations\\nis the local restatement of the parent's eviction bug and is never acceptable.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 7. Concurrency: two locks, deliberately separate\\n\\n| lock | path | held by | protects |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| writer lease | `hot-main/.writer-lease` | the warmer only | the snapshot store and `hot-main/repo` |\\n| full-build lock | `.full-build-lock` | warmer **and** consumers | RAM/CPU: one full `lake build` machine-wide |\\n\\nThey are separate so that a consumer's own full build can proceed while the\\nwarmer sits idle between commits, and so that a warmer holding the writer lease\\ndoes not block a consumer that only wants to *read* a published snapshot.\\n\\n`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They\\nare read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`\\ngate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add\\nlocking there.\\n\\nThe parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that\\na CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice\\n(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale\\nbuild; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.\\n\\nBoth locks use the same mkdir/rename-to-break protocol described in §5.1, with\\nthe same liveness-first staleness rule, so a consumer and the warmer agree on\\nwhat a stale lock is.\\n\\n### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`\\n\\n`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two\\ncompatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:\\n\\n* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,\\n  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to\\n  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override\\n  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the\\n  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the\\n  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,\\n  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see\\n  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)\\n* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO\\n  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.\\n  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude \\\"no pid, therefore\\n  stale\\\" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here\\n  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then\\n  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`\\n  field is read as \\\"this host\\\", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`\\n\\nReplaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s\\nGitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:\\n\\n1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a\\n   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable\\n   error.\\n2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. This document specifies the local replacement for the parent\nworkflow's GitHub Actions build cache, and the rules every worktree must obey to\navoid duplicate compilation. It is the protocol behind three executables:\n\n| script | role |\n|---|---|\n| `local/bin/cache-warmer.sh` | the **single writer**: builds `main`, publishes read-only snapshots |\n| `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh` | the **consumer**: keyhash-gated copy-on-write clone into a worktree |\n| `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` | fresh-worktree bootstrap (replaces `.codex/setup.sh`) |\n\nGoverning invariants: `local/DESIGN.md` #1 (single cache writer) and #7 (one full\n`lake build` machine-wide). Where this document and `DESIGN.md` disagree,\n`DESIGN.md` wins.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What is being replaced, and why it was built that way\n\nThe parent repository's caching design is the residue of a specific, documented\nfailure. The load-bearing citations:\n\n| parent mechanism | citation | what it encodes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Split restore/save, save only on `main` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:137-167` | *\"The cache is saved only from main and restored everywhere.\"* |\n| `lean-action`'s own cache disabled | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:138-142` | The post-mortem: a ~2.6 GB entry saved **per PR run** cycled through the 10 GB repository cache budget and evicted the main-branch entry, *\"so no run ever restored usable MIPStarRE oleans and every run rebuilt the whole library.\"* |\n| Same policy restated in the weekly job | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:75-77` | *\"See pr-ci.yml: per-run lake caches evict the main build cache from the repository cache budget.\"* |\n| Main runs exempt from cancellation | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:50` | *\"Do not cancel main-branch runs: they seed the build cache.\"* |\n| Save runs `if: always()` on main | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:161-162` | *\"Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still spares the next run the modules that did compile.\"* |\n| ProofWidgets prune workaround | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:56-69` | A fresh-tree upstream bug that aborts the entire Mathlib cache fetch |\n| `elan` install isolated from the cache lifecycle | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:44-54` | Avoids *\"a partial cache save or restore-then-overwrite that could are manual only | `.github/workflows/update.yml:3-5` | A bump *\"triggers a full library rebuild and possibly an auto-fix cascade\"* |\n| Lean setup removed from a PR job | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:314` | A job was demoted to a notice *\"after repeated runner disk exhaustion\"* |\n\nThe single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable\ncache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the\nsame failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared\nbuild tree.\n\n---\n\n## 2. The two-tier split\n\n`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and\ndifferent sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the\nparent's failure.\n\nAn absolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` relocates `.lake` to `<root>/<branch>` for a\none-component branch name. The helper rejects `/`, symlink targets, escape, and\ncanonical overlap with packages, `hot-main`, the repository, or any worktree,\nplus canonical-equal ownership by another worktree. Export it before setup or\nwarming and through dispatch and cleanup; only its target gets `--add-dir`.\n\n**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,\n`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the\nparent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and\ndistributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**\ncopy.\n\n**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The\nparent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud\ncache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally they live **once\nper manifest** in a shared, read-only store:\n`$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`, `key = sha256(lake-manifest.json ‖ lean-toolchain)[:16]`,\nand every worktree's `.lake/packages` is a symlink to it.\n\n> **Why a shared store is safe here (2026-09-03).** The old objection — a\n> shared tree is read-only only by convention, so one `lake update` mutates it\n> for everyone — is answered mechanically: the store is `chmod -R a-w`, so any\n> write (an automated `lake update`, a dependency rebuild after a manifest\n> drift) fails loudly in the one worktree that attempted it. Identity is by\n> key, so a Mathlib bump simply creates a new store entry; worktrees on the old\n> manifest keep linking the old one. The first worktree to need a key fetches\n> with `lake exe cache get` into a real directory, then *publishes* it (move,\n> `chmod a-w`, link); later worktrees only link. Cost: 7.3 GB once per key\n> instead of per worktree (8 copies = 58 GB on 2026-09-03, on a 97 % full disk).\n> `worktree-setup.sh` still refuses to run `lake update`.\n\nConsequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It\nrewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under\nevery published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib\nbumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.\n\n---\n\n## 3. The cache key\n\n```\nkeyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )\n```\n\nconcatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local\nanalog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in\n`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`\nand `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay\nbyte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.\nA missing input file is a hard error, never a default.\n\nTwo properties matter, and they are not symmetric:\n\n1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's\n   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest\n   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is\n   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash\n   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not\n   need their timestamps preserved.\n2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,\n   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.\n   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`\n   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls\n   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.\n\n---\n\n## 4. On-disk layout\n\nShared packages and `hot-main` use `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`; branch products may\nuse `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` as in §2. Neither runtime tree is committed.\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/\n├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time\n│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose\n├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends\n├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)\n└── hot-main/\n    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this\n    │   └── info\n    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main\n    ├── snapshots/\n    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    │   │   ├── STAMP\n    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build\n    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink\n```\n\nSnapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse\nlexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`\ncalls and no name parsing.\n\n### `STAMP` schema\n\nA flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts\nparse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase\nhex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever\n`eval`ed or `source`d.\n\n```\nsha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>\nkeyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>\ntimestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>\ntimestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>\nstatus=complete|partial\nbuild_seconds=<integer>\ntoolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>\nsnapshot=<snapshot directory name>\nwarmer_version=1\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]\n                          [--targets \"<lake targets>\"] [--lock-timeout S]\n                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]\n```\n\n### 5.1 Writer lease\n\nAcquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic\ntest-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,\n`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.\n\nStaleness is decided in this order:\n\n* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead\n  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.\n* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).\n\nThe TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this\nrepository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,\n2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease\nmid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to\nprevent.\n\n**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that\nboth judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;\n`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and\nre-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A\n`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.\n\n### 5.2 Build\n\n1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`\n   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.\n   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and\n   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).\n2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).\n3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**\n   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and\n   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,\n   finish, then warm again.\n4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply\n   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.\n   **No `lake update`.**\n5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.\n   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is\n   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent\n   prompts may later read.\n\n### 5.3 Atomic publish\n\nThe publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:\n\n1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with\n   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the\n   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).\n2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.\n3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.\n   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already\n   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**\n4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over\n   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).\n\n> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,\n> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would\n> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real\n> trap, not a hypothetical one.\n\nConsumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the\nresolved concrete path for the rest of the run.\n\n### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional\n\nIf `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and\nexits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`\ncommit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did\ncompile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say\nso loudly.\n\nA non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *\"main did not build cleanly\"* —\nnot *\"nothing was published.\"* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a\nreason to retry.\n\n### 5.5 Retention\n\nKeep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's\n10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never\ncollected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has\nresolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging\ndirectories older than an hour are swept.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]\n                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]\n```\n\nThe consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to\noperate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.\n\nDecision procedure:\n\n1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).\n2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.\n3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. A malformed stamp is treated as *no snapshot*.\n4. **Keyhash gate.** Mismatch → warn with both hashes, name the likely cause\n   (toolchain / manifest / lakefile change), point at the warmer, and take the\n   cold path. Never a partial reuse, never a silent skip.\n5. **Warm path**: `cp -c -R <snapshot>/build → <worktree>/.lake/build.incoming.$$`,\n   then `rename` into place. Write the idempotency marker\n   `<worktree>/.lake/.mipstarre-warm-stamp` recording the snapshot name, keyhash,\n   snapshot status and time. Then fetch tier 2 with `lake exe cache get`.\n   No full build unless `--build` is given — the point of the warm path is that\n   the agent's next incremental `lake build` compiles only its own delta.\n6. **Cold path**: `lake exe cache get`, then a full `lake build` under the\n   machine-wide lock (§7), unless `--no-build`.\n\n### 6.1 Idempotency and the do-not-clobber rule\n\nRe-running on an already-warmed worktree is a no-op for tier 1. Specifically:\n\n* marker snapshot **and** keyhash both match the resolved snapshot → skip the\n  clone;\n* `.lake/build` is populated but was **not** warmed from this snapshot → leave it\n  alone and warn. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it\n  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.\n\n### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink\n\nOn APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near\ninstantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid\nfor only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. This is what makes a\n*private writable copy per worktree* affordable — and a private writable copy is\nprecisely what preserves the single-writer invariant. A writable symlink or\nbind-style share of `.lake/build` across two concurrent `lake build` invocations\nis the local restatement of the parent's eviction bug and is never acceptable.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Concurrency: two locks, deliberately separate\n\n| lock | path | held by | protects |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| writer lease | `hot-main/.writer-lease` | the warmer only | the snapshot store and `hot-main/repo` |\n| full-build lock | `.full-build-lock` | warmer **and** consumers | RAM/CPU: one full `lake build` machine-wide |\n\nThey are separate so that a consumer's own full build can proceed while the\nwarmer sits idle between commits, and so that a warmer holding the writer lease\ndoes not block a consumer that only wants to *read* a published snapshot.\n\n`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They\nare read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`\ngate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add\nlocking there.\n\nThe parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that\na CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice\n(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale\nbuild; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.\n\nBoth locks use the same mkdir/rename-to-break protocol described in §5.1, with\nthe same liveness-first staleness rule, so a consumer and the warmer agree on\nwhat a stale lock is.\n\n### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`\n\n`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two\ncompatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:\n\n* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,\n  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to\n  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override\n  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the\n  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the\n  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,\n  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see\n  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)\n* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO\n  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.\n  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude \"no pid, therefore\n  stale\" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here\n  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then\n  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`\n  field is read as \"this host\", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`\n\nReplaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s\nGitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:\n\n1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a\n   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable\n   error.\n2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is\n   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.\n3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only\n   if the pin is not already installed.\n4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).\n5. **`origin/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a warning, because the hooks and every\n   diff-based audit silently self-disable without it. Silent self-disabling is the\n   documented failure this check exists to surface.\n6. **Fresh-state workaround** (§8.2).\n7. **`warm-worktree.sh`** — invoked from the copy *next to this script*, not the\n   copy inside the worktree being bootstrapped. A worktree may hold an unreviewed\n   branch; the bootstrap must not execute code from the tree it is bootstrapping.\n   This is the local analog of `DESIGN.md` #5 (trusted prompts come from `main`).\n   If the consumer script is missing, this is a **hard error**: without it the\n   worktree would start cold, silently, which is the outcome the whole protocol\n   exists to prevent.\n8. **`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`**, then `--check`. `docs/ci-automation.md`\n   calls out `--check` specifically for *\"each fresh worktree used for a PR.\"*\n\n`--check` is report-only and mutates nothing (`DESIGN.md` #10). It exits non-zero\nif anything is missing.\n\n### 8.1 Git environment hygiene\n\nEvery invocation of `lake` or of `git` inside a vendored package is wrapped in\n`run_outside_git_env`, ported from `.githooks/pre-push:19-25`: it unsets every\nvariable named by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` in a subshell. Without it, a\nscript invoked from inside a git hook leaks `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` into\nLake's package checkouts, and nested git operations resolve the wrong repository.\n\n### 8.2 The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround\n\nKept verbatim in intent from `docgen.yml:56-69`, in all three scripts, because a\npristine agent worktree is exactly the fresh state that triggers it.\n\n*Upstream form.* `lake exe cache get` runs `lake update`, whose mathlib\npost-update hook prunes `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib` before\nfetching a cloud release. On a tree that has never built, the directory does not\nexist, and the uncaught exception aborts the **entire** cache fetch. Fix: create\nthe directory, but only if `proofwidgets` was actually checked out.\n\n*Local form.* The same fetch also aborts when a vendored package tree is\n**dirty**: build byproducts (`widget/js/lake.trace`) block the revision checkout.\nRecorded in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, 2026-08-30 — a failed build followed\nby a successful retry after `git reset --hard` in the package. The scripts\ntherefore reset any vendored package tree with **tracked** modifications before\nfetching.\n\n`git clean` is deliberately **not** run inside a vendored package: it would delete\ndownloaded build output at a cost of hours. If an untracked byproduct still blocks\na checkout, the fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from\nsource.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Telemetry\n\nEvery full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.\n\n```jsonc\n{\"ts\": \"<ISO 8601 with offset>\",\n \"kind\": \"warm\" | \"rebuild\" | \"cache-get\",\n \"trigger\": \"<who asked for this>\",\n \"outcome\": \"success\" | \"failed\",\n \"seconds\": <int>,\n \"sha\": \"<commit, when known>\",\n \"note\": \"<sanitized, ≤400 chars>\"}\n```\n\n* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.\n* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).\n* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.\n\nThree properties are load-bearing:\n\n* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked\n  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the\n  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and\n  produce merge conflicts. Override with `MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR`.\n* **Appends are serialized** by a short-lived `mkdir` lock, and give up after 5 s\n  rather than delaying a build. Telemetry never blocks or fails a build; every\n  failure path degrades to a warning.\n* **`note` is sanitized** — non-printable characters stripped, truncated to 400\n  characters — because notes may quote build output, and compiler output is\n  untrusted text regardless of where it was produced (`DESIGN.md` #6).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Operating procedures\n\n```bash\n# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main\n\n# What is published right now?\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status\n\n# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/.worktrees/issue-0042-qpbt-basis\n\n# Verify an existing worktree without touching it.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check\n\n# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force\n\n# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status\n```\n\nAfter a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm\nfirst, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot\nis invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Run\n`cache-warmer.sh --ref main` before dispatching agents, or pay for a full build in\neach worktree serialized behind one lock.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Failure modes and how each degrades\n\n| condition | behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |\n| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |\n| Malformed / unreadable `STAMP` | Treated as *no snapshot*; cold path. |\n| Snapshot is `partial` | Used, with a warning naming the SHA that failed. |\n| `cp -c` unsupported (non-APFS, cross-volume) | Warn, fall back to `cp -R`. Correct, just slower and larger. |\n| `lake exe cache get` fails | Warn; tier 2 gets compiled from source. Non-fatal. |\n| Full-build lock held | Wait; the warmer waits indefinitely by default, consumers time out per `--lock-timeout`. |\n| Stale lock (dead pid, or age > TTL) | Broken by atomic rename, with a warning naming the dead holder. |\n| Primary repo has no commits on `main` | Hard error naming the cause. Never a silent no-op. |\n| `warm-worktree.sh` missing during bootstrap | Hard error. `--skip-warm` is the explicit opt-out. |\n| `origin/main` does not resolve | Warning, non-zero exit from `--check`, because hooks self-disable silently. |\n| `python3` absent | Warmer: hard error (needed for the atomic publish). Consumer: warning, telemetry skipped. |\n\n---\n\n## 12. What it is\n\nThe parent repository consolidated seven workflows into one so that a pull\nrequest produces exactly **one** CI completion event, which the auto-fix\ndispatcher keys off (`pr-ci.yml:3-8`). The local port keeps that property: one\ninvocation, one manifest, one exit code.\n\n```\nlocal/bin/ci.sh <pr-id> [--worktree PATH] [--base REF] [--only STEP]\n                        [--force-all] [--skip-build] [--dry-run]\n```\n\n`<pr-id>` is the GitHub PR number; the script reads `branch`, `base` and the\nhead SHA from GitHub (`gh_common.py pr-view`), finds the branch's worktree (via\n`git worktree list`, falling back to `.worktrees/<branch with / → ->`), and\nruns everything **inside that worktree**. Nothing is run in the primary\ncheckout, and the worktree's branch tip must equal the remote head before the\nrun starts.\n\nExit status: `0` all gating steps passed or were legitimately skipped; `1` at\nleast one gating step failed or could not run; `2` the run could not start\n(unknown PR number, missing worktree, unresolvable base, GitHub unreachable —\na GitHub error never degrades to a local record).\n\n### Preconditions that are hard errors, never silent skips\n\n| Precondition | Why it is fatal |\n|---|---|\n| GitHub returns an open PR with a head branch | there is no branch to test |\n| a worktree for that branch exists | CI must not test the primary checkout |\n| `origin/<base>` or `<base>` resolves | invariant 8 — the diff-based audits and the change gating self-disable without a base, which is exactly the \"checks silently stopped running\" failure the parent repo patched twice |\n| a merge base exists | the change set is undefined without one |\n| `python3` on `PATH` | every audit job and the manifest writer need it |\n\nThere is deliberately **no `LOCAL_CI_ENABLED` kill switch**. `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED`\nand `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` exist because a disabled reviewer or fixer merely\nstops work from happening; a disabled CI would hand the merge gate a green\nlight it never earned. If CI must not run, do not run it — the head SHA simply\nkeeps whatever statuses it already carries.\n\n## 2. When you widen\n> a scan tree in `scripts/*.py`, widen the matching glob in `ci.sh` in the same\n> commit, per `meta.md` §5.\n\nThe `workflow` area is the one deliberate extension. On GitHub it meant \"the\nworkflow file changed, so re-run everything\"; locally the workflow layer is a\nwhole tree — the frozen reference `pr-ci.yml`, every driver and helper under\n`local/bin/`, every protocol under `local/protocols/`, and the hooks in\n`.githooks/` — and a change to any of them forces a full run, every step\nincluded. The globs are that broad on purpose: a `gh_common.py`-only change has\nto run the `scripts/tests` unit suite that covers it — carried by\n`blueprint-sync` — and under the old three-file glob such a change matched no\narea and ran nothing at all (PR 7 review, F13).\n\n## 4. Manifest schema\n\nBuilt in runtime storage (same-directory tempfile + `os.replace`) and then\nposted as the manifest PR comment (§5):\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.json          complete run\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.partial.json  partial run\n```\n\nA run is **partial** when it was given `--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`;\n`--dry-run` writes nothing at all.\n\nStep logs live outside the repository, under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<pr-id>/<head_sha>/<step>.log`.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"schema\": 1,\n  \"generator\": \"local/bin/ci.sh\",\n  \"replaces\": \".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml\",\n  \"pr\": 7,                       // GitHub PR number\n  \"branch\": \"issue-7-qpbt-basis\",\n  \"base\": \"main\",                // from the GitHub PR\n  \"base_ref\": \"origin/main\",     // what actually resolved\n  \"merge_base\": \"<sha>\",\n  \"head_sha\": \"<sha>\",           // the SHA every step ran against\n  \"worktree\": \"/abs/path\",\n  \"started\": \"2026-08-30T09:23:07+0800\",   // ISO-8601 with offset\n  \"finished\": \"2026-08-30T09:41:52+0800\",\n  \"seconds\": 1125,               // whole run, integer\n  \"conclusion\": \"success\",       // success | failure | error\n  \"partial\": false,              // true ⇒ not a merge-gate verdict\n  \"areas\": { \"lean\": true, \"blueprint_src\": false, ... },\n  \"changed_files\": [\"MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean\", ...],\n  \"warnings\": [\"texra-blueprint not installed; skipped ...\", ...],\n  \"steps\": [\n    {\n      \"step\": \"build\",           // one of the eight job ids, always all eight\n      \"outcome\": \"success\",      // success | failure | error | skipped\n      \"seconds\": 883,\n      \"log_path\": \"/Users/…/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/0007/<sha>/build.log\",\n      \"blocking\": true,\n      \"note\": \"\"                 // skip reason, exit code, or degradation cause\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nOutcome vocabulary — the distinction is what routes the auto-fix loop:\n\n| `outcome` | Meaning | Auto-fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| `success` | the step ran and passed | — |\n| `failure` | the step ran and the code is wrong | `build` → ci-fix, `blueprint-render` → blueprint-fix, everything else → **never** |\n| `error` | the step could not run (missing tool, unbootstrapped worktree, build lock unavailable) | never — this is an operator problem, not a code problem |\n| `skipped` | gated out, or excluded by `--only` / `--skip-build` | — |\n\n`conclusion` is `failure` if any step failed, else `error` if any step errored,\nelse `success`. The run's exit status is `0` iff `conclusion == \"success\"`.\n\n## 5. Publication\n\nEvidence goes to GitHub, bound to the exact SHA the steps ran against\n(`issues-prs.md` §2). For every complete run:\n\n* one `local-ci/<step>` status per gate step — `pending` posted before the\n  step, then `success | failure | error`; a gated-out step is a `success`\n  whose description says it was skipped, so the gate never has to distinguish\n  \"absent\" from \"not applicable\";\n* `local-ci/summary` carrying the run's `conclusion`;\n* the manifest JSON as the PR comment marked\n  `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, created or updated in place.\n\n`pending` before the first step is the old `ci_status: running`: a crashed,\nkilled or power-cut run leaves `pending`, never a stale `success`, so the\nreview gate's \"green CI on the same head SHA\" check (invariant 2) fails closed.\nImmediately before the final publication `ci.sh` re-reads both the local branch\ntip and the remote PR head; if either moved, it publishes no success and exits\nnonzero, because a status is a claim about one commit.\n\nA **partial** run (`--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`) publishes nothing at\nall — no statuses, no manifest comment — and keeps its manifest in runtime\nstorage only. `--base` belongs on that list because an overridden base (the PR\nhead, say) can empty the diff and mark every gate skipped-success. Partial runs\nare a debugging aid; they must not be able to produce a merge-gate verdict, and\nthey must not clobber a complete manifest for the same SHA.\n\n## 6. Concurrency and locks\n\nTwo advisory `mkdir`-based lease directories, both under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/` (`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` overrides the root). Each\nholds an `owner` file: pid, ISO timestamp, tag. A lock is broken only when its\nowner pid is dead or its stamp is older than `MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S`\n(default 3 h).\n\n| Lock | Scope | On contention |\n|---|---|---|\n| `locks/ci-<pr-id>.lock` | one `ci.sh` per PR | **refuse immediately** (exit 2) |\n| `$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock` | one full `lake build` machine-wide (invariant 7) | wait up to `MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S` (default 4 h), then record `build` as `error` and continue with the Python steps |\n\nOnly the `build` step takes the full-build lock. The audits are pure Python and\ntake nothing; single-file `lake env lean` checks are read-only over oleans and\ntake nothing either — which is precisely why `.githooks/pre-push` can use them\nper-file without serializing.\n\n`ci.sh` never cancels a running build. GitHub cancels in-progress PR runs\n(`pr-ci.yml:48-51`) because its runners are disposable and main-branch runs —\nthe ones that seed the cache — are exempt. Locally there is nothing disposable:\nkilling a build mid-flight leaves a half-written `.lake/build` and a held lease.\nSo a second run for the same PR is refused, and a foreign live build lease is\nwaited on, never stolen. Do not `kill -9` a running `ci.sh`; if you must, remove\nthe lease directories by hand.\n\n## 7. Build step and the two-tier cache\n\n`build` is the only step that touches the cache, and it only ever **reads** the\nshared tree. This is the local translation of the parent's main-only cache save\npolicy, whose rationale is documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142`: per-PR saves of\n~2.6 GB cycled through the 10 GB repository budget and evicted the main entry,\nso no run ever restored usable oleans. The local failure mode is identical if a\nworktree writes into the shared snapshot, so it does not.\n\n1. If `.lake/build` is absent, run `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh <worktree>`,\n   which resolves the hot-main snapshot and clones it copy-on-write. Contract:\n   idempotent, exit 0 when it populated or deliberately declined, nonzero on a\n   hard error.\n   - warmer missing → loud warning, cold build (still correct, just slow);\n     set `MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1` to make it an `error` instead.\n2. `.lake/build` (this project's oleans, per-worktree, writable) and\n   `.lake/packages` (Mathlib and friends) are **different tiers** and are never\n   conflated. If `.lake/packages` is a symlink it points at the shared hot-main\n   dependency tree and is read-only: `lake exe cache get` is **skipped**,\n   because it writes there. If it is a real directory, `lake exe cache get`\n   runs, mirroring what `lean-action` does inside the parent job. Never run\n   `lake update` in a consumer worktree.\n3. `.lake/packages` absent entirely → `error`, pointing at\n   `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`. That bootstrap path is where the ProofWidgets\n   prune workaround lives, and a package-free tree is exactly the state that\n   triggers it. `MIPSTARRE_CI_ALLOW_COLD_FETCH=1` overrides for a tree you know\n   is clean.\n4. `lake build`, then `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`, then the\n   comparator drift check.\n\nEvery `lake` and `python3` invocation goes through a subshell that unsets\n`git rev-parse --local-env-vars` first. Inherited `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`\nmake Lake resolve nested package repositories against the wrong repository;\n`.githooks/pre-push:19-24` does the same thing for the same reason, and any\norchestrator that invokes `ci.sh` from inside a git hook inherits the problem.\n\nLake's staleness is trace-hash-based, not mtime-based, so a restored snapshot\nolder than the merge base is safe — but only within one\n`hash(lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, lakefile.toml)` class. Crossing that\nboundary is `build-cache.md`'s problem, not this protocol's: `ci.sh` delegates\nthe check to `warm-worktree.sh` and simply builds whatever it is handed.\n\n## 8. The axiom audit is reported, not run\n\n`blueprint-sync` deliberately has no Lean setup. On GitHub that was forced by\nrepeated runner disk exhaustion, and the job degraded to a `::notice` telling a\nhuman to run the audit locally (`pr-ci.yml:303-317`). Locally the constraint is\ndifferent but the conclusion is the same: the machine has a single full-build\nbudget, already spent by `build`. So `blueprint_axiom_audit_needed.py` runs, and\nwhen it answers `true` the run records a warning:\n\n> run `python3 scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py --ci` in a Lean environment\n\nDe-automation of this kind is a legitimate evolution step (`meta.md` §4), and\nthis one is inherited rather than invented.\n\n## 9. Telemetry\n\nWhen `build` actually ran (any outcome but `skipped`), one line is appended to\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`:\n\n```json\n{\"ts\":\"…\",\"kind\":\"ci-build\",\"trigger\":\"ci.sh pr=0007\",\"seconds\":883,\n \"outcome\":\"success\",\"sha\":\"…\",\"note\":\"branch issue-7-qpbt-basis\"}\n```\n\nThis satisfies the `meta.md` duty that every full build be accounted for, and\nmakes \"how much wall time did CI cost this PR\" answerable by a script. The\nper-step seconds in the manifest are the finer-grained record.\n\n## 10. Trust boundary\n\nTwo things about `ci.sh` are worth stating plainly.\n\n**It executes branch-authored code.** The audit scripts, the test suite, and\n`lakefile.toml` all come from the worktree under test, because that is what CI\nmeans and what the parent workflow did. Never run `ci.sh` on a branch you would\nnot run a shell script from.\n\n**Its logs are untrusted data.** Compiler diagnostics, plasTeX output and test\nfailures can contain arbitrary text, including text shaped like instructions.\n`ci.sh` stores logs verbatim and makes no attempt to clean them. Any consumer\nthat feeds a log into an agent prompt — `autofix.sh` above all — owes the\nsanitization required by invariant 6: strip control characters, break fences,\ntruncate, and frame the payload as data that must not be followed. The manifest\ngives consumers `log_path` rather than log content precisely so this stays the\nconsumer's explicit, visible responsibility.\n\n## 11. Amendments\n\nChanging a gating glob, a step's command set, the manifest schema, the status\ncontexts or their vocabulary, or a lock's name or semantics is an amendment:\nrecord the trigger in `results/telemetry/events.md`, edit this file and\n`ci.sh` together, append to `EVOLUTION.md`, and grep `local/` for every other\nenforcement point (`meta.md` §5).
